--- Page 1 (Beckerman_26a) --- Dear Jack, These last two days' mail have brought your letters of March 25-27-which were of course very welcome. Sorry to hear that air mail is slowing up in your direction - we'll try putting through a V-mail this week to see if that goes with any more speed. We do know that when Abe writes V-mail they always arrive later than his letters - but that may have no bearing. . . . Glad to hear that everything is going along well - too well you say; that leaves us no room for any kind of worry. . . . By the way we think that anonymous package you received is more likely from Uncle Ben and Sarah - as we sent them your address some time ago. That's just to get the "Thank you's" straightened out. . . . Passing Mintz's candy store the other day we noticed a familiar looking face that was grinning very broadly, peering out from an enlarged newspaper picture that was pasted in the window. Looking [illegible] we recognized "Bake" who was --- Page 2 (Beckerman_26b) --- II shown Reading a column of captured prisoners. That stood out most was that mile wide gun & the picture was very aptly headed 'A Happy G.I.' I think you'll send in the next Bull The biggest news from here reverts back again to the 'Coops'. He thought we had written you the closing chapter last time but since then the situation has been reversed and the happy ending has been unwillingly exchanged for the contrary. He wrote you last that a raise in rent was going to supply the needed money, but the company has once more increased their demands and this time the sum is too high to consider paying it. So what we've tried to prevent for so long has happened - the mortgage company has already taken over and are represented by a "receiver" in the office. No one however was going to accept that fact too readily - Section committees were formed & meetings held, and it was unanimously decided not to payment. Court proceedings, evictions & other legal technicalities were supposed to follow if that plan was carried through. That's all in the past tense because a [illegible] meeting yesterday --- Page 3 (Beckerman_26c) --- The "Emergency tenants' committee," as its now called, met with representatives of the comp. and laid down a series of demands - all of which were granted. That all cultural facilities - clubs, library, pool, and etc. - remain under the jurisdiction of the Tenants Committee, that the entire staff be kept on, including the cultural director. So that's exactly how things stand now, we're paying rent again, only it's now going to other coffers. We're all glad that everything is remaining intact otherwise, as what we feared most was having those facilities being turned into 'Apartments for Late Rent'! News of no how is about the same - all feeling all right. Summer is approaching and we're on the lookout for some country peace to where Papa can go & have a restful vacation for the 2 months - Mama too of course. Prices for such rooms have tripled in the last year, but money would be no obstacle if we could find a nice place. We're able hoping to be able to desert the city this summer making out letters of application. --- Page 4 (Beckerman_26d) --- different camps for a job as a counselor there the money goes to the other extreme now down - but they're pretty particular in most places I've found, experience seems to be the keynote. There's always the alternative of going to summer school and looking at figures in the office, but 10 months a yr. of that routine makes the other more attractive. Well, we all hope it will be "back to nature"! It's just been back to life. again for our bike as a new front inner and outer tire completed its rehabilitation program. Now at least we don't feel as if it's just dead weight around. That's about all there is for tonight. Excuse the ink blots, fed the pen too much. Love - Regards from all mama Papa Ruth
